solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: My tip to thrill in headwear for Ascot?

indicators.note: a tip is the very end or point of something, so only the leading letter is wanted
one thing placed in another sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: the opening letter of thrill
racegoers at Royal Ascot famously wear elaborate hats

explanation.surface: Someone at Royal Ascot is thrilled by a fancy hat.
explanation.walkthrough: Royal Ascot is an English horse-race meeting known for extravagant hats. 'My' looks like part of the sentence but is the whole definition, an exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild exclamations of surprise, interchangeable when someone hears unexpected news.

clue.text: A Pole employed by one casting Hook?

definitions.text: A Pole employed by one casting Hook?

blocks.clueFragment: A Pole employed by one casting Hook?
blocks.note: surface reading: a Polish actor hired by a director casting the pirate Captain Hook

blocks.clueFragment: A Pole employed by one casting Hook?
blocks.note: setter's reading: a pole used by an angler who casts a hook into the water

explanation.walkthrough: The capitals do the misleading: Pole reads as a Polish person and Hook as the Peter Pan pirate, but they are an ordinary pole and a fish hook.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler casts a line with baited hook using a long flexible pole, which is exactly this piece of tackle.

clue.text: Pointers annoy grannies ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is taken

blocks.note: to needle someone is to irritate them
the closing letter of grannies

explanation.surface: Pointers on a dial or display irritate elderly people in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: Grannies suggests knitting needles, which helps the surface, but the word only supplies its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The moving indicators on gauges, compasses and dials are called by this name as well as pointers.

clue.text: Agreeable blokes leaving southern state

indicators.note: something leaving departs, so that letter is dropped from the word

blocks.note: yes-men agree with everything their boss says
S is the standard abbreviation for southern

explanation.surface: Pleasant men are moving out of a southern state of the USA.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Southern state' looks like one phrase, perhaps Alabama or Georgia, but southern belongs to the wordplay and state alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a country on the Arabian Peninsula, and a sovereign country is a state.

clue.text: Senior on drugs charged along with royal

blocks.note: someone on drugs is high
charged in the sense of rushed forward
a king is a royal

explanation.surface: An elderly person on drugs was charged by police along with a member of the royal family.
explanation.walkthrough: Charged suggests a criminal charge, but it means ran at speed, as a bull charges.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior officer or official holds an elevated position in a hierarchy, the meaning of the adjective.

clue.text: Duck left out for afternoon munchies

indicators.note: out means removed or excluded, so that letter goes

blocks.note: the teal is a small wild duck
L is the usual abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A duck is left out as an afternoon snack.
explanation.walkthrough: Duck could be a verb, to dodge, but here it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain the light meal of sandwiches and cake eaten mid-afternoon is called by this name, so it covers snacks.

clue.text: Summer’s beginning, pack and go away

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter alone

blocks.note: the first letter of summer
to cram is to pack tightly

explanation.surface: At the start of summer, someone packs a case and heads off on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'and' joins wordplay to definition rather than listing two actions.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a slangy imperative telling someone to leave at once, the same as the command go away.

clue.text: Does nothing get Satan annoyed with saint?

indicators.note: someone annoyed is stirred up, so these letters are disturbed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
S is an abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A question: does doing nothing make the devil cross with a holy man?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get' reads as part of the sentence's grammar, but its letters are needed in the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A pond or economy that stagnates stays still and makes no progress, so it is inactive.

clue.text: Don’t dash as much as one out on first delivery

blocks.note: first meaning: an instruction to sprint less often, split into two words
second meaning: a cricket batter dismissed by the first ball bowled has scored nothing

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a delivery is one ball bowled; a batter out first ball has no score. Read as two words the answer is also advice to slow down.
explanation.definitionFit: A batter dismissed by the opening ball has no runs, while the split phrase literally means sprint less.

clue.text: Fable teacher read out loud with a lisp

indicators.note: reading out loud means we judge the word by its sound rather than its spelling
a lisp turns every S sound into a TH sound when spoken

blocks.note: a schoolteacher is addressed as Miss, which a lisp turns into Mith

explanation.surface: A teacher reads a fable aloud to a class while lisping.
explanation.walkthrough: Pupils call a female teacher Miss; lisped, the final S becomes TH.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional story of gods or heroes, like a fable, is a legendary tale not literally true.

clue.text: Heated issue involving small group of players

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a team is a group of players

explanation.surface: A hotly debated matter involves a small band of sportspeople or musicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heated issue' suggests a controversy, but it is what issues from heated water.
explanation.definitionFit: Water vapour pours out of a boiling kettle, so the vapour is literally an emission produced by heating.

clue.text: Be unfavourable to have another shot (extremely skint)

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the two outermost letters

blocks.note: to have another go or attempt
the first and last letters of skint

explanation.surface: Being broke makes it a bad idea to have another bet or turn.
explanation.walkthrough: Skint is British slang for having no money; only its outside letters are used.
explanation.definitionFit: When a ruling or result goes against you it turns out badly for you, so the phrase means work to someone's disadvantage.

clue.text: A run enlivened with changes taxes people

indicators.note: changes alter the arrangement, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tax reform has livened up a sporting run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taxes' looks like a verb, but 'taxes people' is a noun phrase: the people who collect taxes. This was the name of the UK tax authority until 2005.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the British government department that collected income tax, so its staff were literally the tax collectors.

clue.text: US tourists provided with no visa react badly

indicators.note: doing something badly leaves it in disorder, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: American travellers react angrily on being turned away without a visa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'US' signals the American word: in Britain these people are holidaymakers.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans call a holiday a vacation, so people away on one are the US equivalent of holidaymakers.

clue.text: Those who mesmerize pythons sit uneasily

indicators.note: something sitting uneasily is unsettled, so these letters are disturbed

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Snakes that charm their prey cannot keep still.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a full sentence about snakes; 'Those who mesmerize' are the subject only for the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Entertainers or therapists who put subjects into a trance are said to mesmerize, after Franz Mesmer.

clue.text: A second month in profit for energy supplier

indicators.note: being in something means lying inside it, so these pieces sit within the other

blocks.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for second
M is the abbreviation for month
a gain is a profit

explanation.surface: Within a month a company reaps a profit as an energy supplier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A second month' sounds like February, but it breaks into three tiny pieces: A, second and month.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the large underground pipe that carries fuel to homes, so it supplies energy.

clue.text: Doctor can treat surrounding area easily

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are altered in order
to surround is to enclose, so one piece goes around another

blocks.note: taken as written
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A doctor can treat the area around a wound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the subject of the sentence, a medic, but it is a verb meaning tamper.
explanation.definitionFit: A canter is a horse's easy gait, so winning this way means comfortably and without effort.

clue.text: Charlie had spades thanks to chap in plot

blocks.note: Charlie is C in the radio alphabet
had a meal, ate
S is the card-game abbreviation for spades
by means of, thanks to

explanation.surface: A man called Charlie got a lot of spades, thanks to a fellow in a garden plot.
explanation.walkthrough: Plot suggests a vegetable patch, matching the spades, but it is the 1605 Gunpowder Plot to blow up Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Catesby led the conspirators of the Gunpowder Plot, so he is a man involved in that famous conspiracy.

clue.text: Old sails and stuff by a Michigan craft

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
a ship's rig is its masts, sails and ropes
taken as written
MI is the postal code for Michigan

explanation.surface: Old sails and gear belonging to a boat from Michigan.
explanation.walkthrough: Craft wants to be a boat, fitting the sails, but it means a handicraft.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper folding is a traditional Japanese handicraft, so it is an art or skill of making things.

clue.text: Dispose of popular Conservative policy

blocks.note: something popular is in
C is the abbreviation for Conservative
a party line is its policy

explanation.surface: A call to scrap a well-liked Tory policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dispose of' reads as a phrase meaning get rid of, but dispose alone is the definition, in the sense of make someone willing.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispose someone towards an idea is to make them inclined towards it; the verbs are synonyms in that sense.

clue.text: Spooner delivers Trump/Brown nuclear deal

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts are exchanged

blocks.note: to trump is to best; it takes the T from the second word
tan is a shade of brown; it takes the B from the first word

explanation.surface: A deal on nuclear weapons brokered between Donald Trump and Gordon Brown.
explanation.walkthrough: Trump and Brown look like political leaders, but are a verb meaning beat and a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A treaty forbidding trial detonations of atomic weapons is an international agreement about nuclear arms.

clue.text: Retirement cover void? Racketeers essentially!

indicators.note: the essence of something is its core, so the central letters are kept

blocks.note: a void is a blank
the two middle letters of racketeers

explanation.surface: A pension or insurance cover is worthless: crooks are behind it.
explanation.walkthrough: Retirement here is going to bed, not leaving work, so the cover is bedding.
explanation.definitionFit: When you retire for the night you sleep under bedding, and this woollen layer is one such covering.

clue.text: What could make killer become kinder?

definitions.text: What could make killer become kinder?

blocks.clueFragment: What could make killer become kinder?
blocks.note: surface reading: what might turn a murderer into a gentler person, a moral conversion

blocks.clueFragment: What could make killer become kinder?
blocks.note: setter's reading: swapping the central letters of the word killer, LL for ND, turns it into kinder

explanation.walkthrough: Heart in crosswords often means the middle letters of a word; replace the middle of killer and you spell kinder.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a reversal of attitude or feelings, and literally replacing the core letters of one word.

clue.text: Harsh critic of head of state after Panama?

indicators.note: coming after means following on, so this piece is placed second

blocks.note: a Panama is a straw hat
ER, Elizabeth Regina, was the Queen, Britain's head of state

explanation.surface: A fierce critic of a country's leader in the wake of events in Panama.
explanation.walkthrough: Panama looks like the country, fitting head of state, but it is a straw hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Online slang uses the word for someone relentlessly negative about another person, a harsh fault-finder.

clue.text: Grouse and cattle reared for their meat

blocks.note: first meaning: a complaint or grievance
second meaning: cows and bullocks kept for butchering

explanation.walkthrough: Grouse alongside cattle reads as the game bird, but it means a grumble.
explanation.definitionFit: It is slang for a complaint, and also names cattle raised for slaughter rather than dairy.

clue.text: Being old is stressful with son turning 100

indicators.note: turning into something means becoming it, so one letter is swapped for another

blocks.note: ex means former or old
taken as written
a tense situation is stressful
S is the abbreviation for son
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: Getting old is hard, especially when your son reaches a hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being old' reads as one phrase about age, but Being alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being as a noun means the state of living or having reality, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Problem with runaway soprano … go on

indicators.note: a runaway has fled, so that letter is no longer present

blocks.note: a snag is a problem
S is the abbreviation for soprano

explanation.surface: Trouble with a singer who walked out, and the show must continue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go on' looks like an encouragement to continue, but it means keep complaining.
explanation.definitionFit: To go on at someone is to keep pestering them with repeated complaints, an idiom matching this verb.

clue.text: Bears steal last piece from hampers

indicators.note: the last piece of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: to take is to steal
the final letter of hampers

explanation.surface: Bears pinch food from picnic baskets, like Yogi Bear.
explanation.walkthrough: Bears looks like the animals, but it is a verb, as in bears the strain.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who bears a burden or pain endures it, and a beam that takes a load supports it.

clue.text: Father always more able to do as he will?

definitions.text: more able to do as he will

blocks.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever

explanation.surface: Is a priest always freer to follow his own will?
explanation.walkthrough: E'er is a poetic form of ever, meaning always, with the apostrophe dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of free describes someone less constrained, better placed to act on their own wishes.

clue.text: Good satirist’s broadcast getting complaint

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered, so these letters are spread into a new order

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
taken as written

explanation.surface: A good satirical programme on air draws a viewer complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: Complaint suggests a grievance about the broadcast, but it is the medical sense, an ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflammation of the stomach lining is an illness, and complaint is a standard word for a bodily ailment.
